summary: This mishnah teaches what makes a sukkah not kosher: if it is too tall, too short, has fewer than three walls, or has more sun than shade. It also teaches about an "old sukkah" built long before the chag.

chunks.he: סֻכָּה שֶׁהִיא גְבוֹהָה לְמַעְלָה מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה,
chunks.en: A sukkah that is taller than twenty amos
chunks.st: A sukka, i.e., its roofing, which is the main and most crucial element of the mitzva, that is more than twenty cubits high

words.note: An amah is a measure, about the length of an arm from elbow to fingertip.

chunks.en: is not kosher. Rabbi Yehuda says it is kosher.
chunks.st: is unfit. Rabbi Yehuda deems it fit.

chunks.en: And one that is not ten tefachim tall,
chunks.st: Similarly, a sukka that is not even ten handbreadths high,

words.note: A tefach is a handbreadth, the width of a hand.

chunks.en: and one that does not have three walls,
chunks.st: and one that does not have three walls,

words.en: and one that does not have

chunks.en: and one that has more sun than shade,
chunks.st: and one whose sunlight that passes through its roofing is greater than its shade

chunks.en: is not kosher. An old sukkah:
chunks.st: are unfit. With regard to an old sukka,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say it is not kosher,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai deem it unfit for the mitzva of sukka

words.note: Beis Shammai are the students of the great Sage Shammai.

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel say it is kosher.
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel deem it fit.

words.note: Beis Hillel are the students of the great Sage Hillel.

chunks.en: And what is an old sukkah?
chunks.st: And which is considered an old sukka?

chunks.he: כָּל שֶׁעֲשָׂאָהּ קֹדֶם לֶחָג שְׁלשִׁים יוֹם.
chunks.en: Any sukkah made thirty days before the chag.
chunks.explain: It was not made for the mitzvah, but for something else.
chunks.st: It is any booth that one established thirty days or more prior to the Festival
chunks.stMore: without expressly designating that it was for the mitzva of sukka. In that case, the assumption is that he constructed it for some other purpose.

chunks.en: But if he made it for the sake of the chag,
chunks.st: However, if he established it expressly for the sake of the festival of Sukkot,

chunks.en: even at the start of the year, it is kosher.
chunks.st: even if he constructed it at the beginning of the previous year, it is fit for use in the fulfillment of the mitzva of sukka, even according to Beit Shammai.

summary: A sukkah under a tree or under another sukkah is not kosher, because its s'chach must be open to the sky. Rabbi Yehuda says when no one can live in the top sukkah, the bottom one is kosher.

chunks.en: Someone who makes his sukkah under a tree,
chunks.st: With regard to one who establishes his sukka beneath a tree,

chunks.en: it is as if he made it inside the house.
chunks.st: it is as though he established it inside the house

chunks.en: A sukkah on top of a sukkah:
chunks.st: If one established a sukka atop another sukka,

chunks.en: the top one is kosher,
chunks.st: the upper sukka is fit

chunks.en: and the bottom one is not kosher.
chunks.st: and the lower sukka is unfit.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: if no one can live in the top one,
chunks.explain: Its floor is too weak to hold people and their things.
chunks.st: If there are no residents in the upper sukka,

chunks.en: the bottom one is kosher.
chunks.st: the lower sukka is fit.

summary: If you spread a sheet over or under the s'chach, or sit under a canopy bed, that spot is not kosher for the sukkah. A low two-post bed cover is allowed.

chunks.en: If he spread a sheet over it because of the sun,
chunks.st: If one spread a sheet over the roofing as protection for those sitting in the sukka due to the sun,

chunks.en: or under it, because of falling leaves,
chunks.st: or if one spread a sheet beneath the roofing as protection due to the falling leaves,

chunks.he: אוֹ שֶׁפֵּרַס עַל גַּבֵּי הַקִּינוֹף, פְּסוּלָה.
chunks.en: or if he spread it over a canopy bed, it is not kosher.
chunks.st: or if one spread a sheet as a canopy over the frame of a four-post [kinof] bed, the area in the sukka beneath the sheets is unfit.
chunks.stMore: In the first two cases, because the sheet is susceptible to ritual impurity, it renders the otherwise fit roofing unfit. In the case of the canopy, one is not sitting under the roofing of the sukka; rather, he is sitting inside a tent.

words.note: A bed with four posts and a cover on top, like a little tent.

chunks.he: אֲבָל פּוֹרֵס הוּא עַל גַּבֵּי נַקְלִיטֵי הַמִּטָּה:
chunks.en: But he may spread it over a bed with two posts.
chunks.explain: Its cover slopes down like a roof, so it is not a real tent.
chunks.st: However, one may spread the sheet over the frame of a two-post [naklitei] bed, which has one post in the middle of each end of the bed. When spreading the sheet over the posts it forms an inclined rather than a flat roof, and a tent with an inclined roof is not considered a significant structure.

words.note: One post at the head and one at the foot of the bed.

summary: Plants still growing from the ground may not be used as s'chach. The rule is: s'chach must grow from the ground and must not be something that can become tamei.

chunks.he: הִדְלָה עָלֶיהָ אֶת הַגֶּפֶן וְאֶת הַדְּלַעַת
chunks.en: If he let a grapevine or a gourd plant climb over it
chunks.st: If one trellised climbing plants such as a grapevine, or gourd plant,

chunks.en: or ivy, and put s'chach on top of them,
chunks.explain: The plants are still attached to the ground.
chunks.st: or ivy [kissos], over a sukka while they were still attached to the ground, and then added roofing atop them,

words.note: S'chach is the covering on top of a sukkah.

chunks.he: פְּסוּלָה. וְאִם הָיָה סִכּוּךְ הַרְבֵּה מֵהֶן,
chunks.en: it is not kosher. But if there was more s'chach than plants,
chunks.st: the sukka is unfit. If the amount of fit roofing was greater than the plants attached to the ground,

chunks.en: or he cut them,
chunks.st: or if he cut the climbing plants so that they were no longer attached to the ground,

chunks.en: it is kosher. This is the rule:
chunks.st: it is fit. This is the principle with regard to the roofing of a sukka:

chunks.en: anything that can become tamei
chunks.st: Anything that is susceptible to ritual impurity, e.g., vessels,

words.note: Tumah is a kind of spiritual impurity.

chunks.en: or does not grow from the ground,
chunks.st: or its growth is not from the ground, e.g., animal hides,

chunks.en: may not be used as s'chach.
chunks.st: one may not roof his sukka with it.

chunks.en: And anything that cannot
chunks.st: And anything that is not

chunks.en: become tamei and grows from the ground,
chunks.st: susceptible to ritual impurity and its growth is from the ground,

chunks.en: may be used as s'chach.
chunks.st: one may roof his sukka with it.

summary: Tied bundles of straw, wood or twigs may not be used as s'chach. Once they are untied they are kosher, and even tied they are fine for walls.

chunks.en: Bundles of straw and bundles of wood
chunks.st: One may not roof a sukka with bundles of straw tied with rope, or bundles of wood,

chunks.en: and bundles of twigs may not be used as s'chach.
chunks.explain: This is when they are tied up.
chunks.st: or bundles of twigs.

chunks.en: And all of them, if he untied them,
chunks.st: And with regard to all of the bundles, if one untied them,

chunks.en: are kosher. And all of them are kosher for walls.
chunks.st: they are fit for use in roofing the sukka, as their lack of fitness is due to the fact that the bundles are tied. And even when tied, all of the bundles are fit for use in constructing the walls of the sukka.

summary: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Meir argue about using boards as s'chach. A wide board on a sukkah is fine, but one may not sleep under it.

chunks.en: We may use boards as s'chach,
chunks.st: One may roof the sukka with boards like those used in the ceiling of a house;

chunks.en: says Rabbi Yehuda.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: And Rabbi Meir forbids it.
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir prohibits their use.

chunks.en: If he put on it a board that is
chunks.st: If one placed a board that is

chunks.en: four tefachim wide,
chunks.st: four handbreadths wide atop the sukka,

chunks.en: it is kosher, as long as he does not sleep under it.
chunks.st: the sukka is fit. He fulfills his obligation, provided he does not sleep beneath the board.

summary: A ceiling of boards with no plaster on top can become a kosher sukkah. Beis Shammai, Beis Hillel and Rabbi Meir argue about what one must do to fix it.

chunks.en: A ceiling of boards that has no plaster on it:
chunks.st: In the case of a roof made of boards that are four handbreadths wide upon which there is no coat of plaster,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says
chunks.stMore: that Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel disagree with regard to the manner in which to render it fit.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: he moves each board and takes out one from between each two.
chunks.explain: He puts kosher s'chach in its place.
chunks.st: One moves each board, and then it is considered as though he placed the board there for the sake of the mitzva of sukka, and one then removes one board from among the boards and replaces it with fit roofing.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: he moves them or takes out one from between.
chunks.st: One need not perform both actions; rather, one must either move the boards or remove one from among them.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: he takes out one from between,
chunks.st: One only removes one from among them

chunks.en: and does not need to move them.
chunks.st: and does not move the others.

summary: Metal spits or bed boards on a sukkah are fine if there are equal spaces between them filled with kosher s'chach. A hole dug into a stack of grain is not a sukkah.

chunks.he: הַמְקָרֶה סֻכָּתוֹ בְשַׁפּוּדִין אוֹ בַאֲרֻכּוֹת הַמִּטָּה,
chunks.en: Someone who roofs his sukkah with spits or with the long boards of a bed,
chunks.st: In the case of one who roofs his sukka with metal skewers or with the long boards of the bed,

words.note: Long metal sticks used for roasting meat.

chunks.en: if the space between them is as wide as they are,
chunks.explain: And he puts kosher s'chach in the spaces.
chunks.st: if there is space between each one of them equal to the width of the skewers or the boards, and if he places fit roofing in those spaces,

chunks.he: כְּשֵׁרָה. הַחוֹטֵט בְּגָדִישׁ לַעֲשׂוֹת בּוֹ סֻכָּה,
chunks.en: it is kosher. Someone who digs into a stack of grain to make a sukkah in it,
chunks.st: the sukka is fit. In the case of one who hollows out and creates a space inside a stack of grain, to construct a sukka in it

chunks.en: it is not a sukkah.
chunks.explain: The roof was not made; it was there already.
chunks.st: it is not a sukka.

summary: Walls that hang down from the top must come within three tefachim of the ground. Walls built up from the ground must be ten tefachim tall. The s'chach must not be three tefachim away from the walls.

chunks.en: Someone who hangs walls from the top down,
chunks.st: One who lowers the walls of the sukka from up downward,

chunks.he: אִם גָּבוֹהַּ מִן הָאָרֶץ שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים, פְּסוּלָה.
chunks.en: if the wall is three tefachim above the ground, it is not kosher.
chunks.explain: Animals could go in under the wall.
chunks.st: if the lower edge of the wall is three handbreadths above the ground, the sukka is unfit.
chunks.stMore: Since animals can enter through that space, it is not the wall of a fit sukka.

chunks.en: From the bottom up,
chunks.st: However, if one constructs the wall from down upward,

chunks.he: אִם גָּבוֹהַּ מִן הָאָרֶץ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים, כְּשֵׁרָה.
chunks.en: if the wall is ten tefachim high from the ground, it is kosher.
chunks.st: if the wall is ten handbreadths high, even if it does not reach the roofing, the sukka is fit.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: just as from the bottom up it must be ten tefachim,
chunks.st: Just as a wall built from down upward must be ten handbreadths,

chunks.en: so from the top down it must be ten tefachim.
chunks.st: so too, in a case where one lowers the wall from up downward, it must be ten handbreadths in length.
chunks.stMore: Regardless of its height off the ground, it is the wall of a fit sukka, as the legal status of a ten-handbreadth partition is that of a full-fledged partition in all areas of halakha.

chunks.en: If he put the s'chach away from
chunks.st: If one distanced the roofing from the walls

chunks.en: the walls by three tefachim, it is not kosher.
chunks.st: of the sukka at a distance of three handbreadths the sukka is unfit, because three handbreadths of open space, even adjacent to the walls, render the sukka unfit.

summary: If the s'chach is far from the walls, with a regular roof in between, the sukkah is kosher only if the gap is less than four amos. The same is true for a big sukkah with bad s'chach around its edges.

chunks.en: A house whose roof broke, and he put s'chach over the hole,
chunks.st: In the case of a house that was breached, creating a hole in the middle of the roof, and one roofed over the breach,

chunks.en: if from the wall
chunks.st: if from the wall

chunks.en: to the s'chach there are four amos, it is not kosher.
chunks.explain: If it is less than four amos, the sukkah is kosher.
chunks.st: to the roofing there are four or more cubits of the remaining original roof, it is an unfit sukka.
chunks.stMore: If the roofing is less than four cubits from the wall, the sukka is fit, based on the principle of curved wall; the remaining intact ceiling is considered an extension of the vertical wall.

chunks.en: And the same for a yard with a porch roof around it.
chunks.st: And likewise, in the case of a courtyard that is surrounded on three sides by a portico,
chunks.stMore: which has a roof but no walls, if one placed roofing over the courtyard between the different sides of the portico and the roof of the portico is four cubits wide, the sukka is unfit.

words.note: A roof held up by posts, with no walls.

chunks.en: A big sukkah
chunks.st: Similarly, a large sukka

chunks.en: that had something around it that may not be used as s'chach,
chunks.st: that was surrounded at the edge of its roofing with material with which one may not roof a sukka, e.g., vessels susceptible to ritual impurity,

chunks.he: אִם יֵשׁ תַּחְתָּיו אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת, פְּסוּלָה:
chunks.en: if there are four amos under it, it is not kosher.
chunks.st: if there are four cubits beneath the unfit roofing, the sukka is unfit. The principle of curved wall does not apply to unfit roofing that measures four cubits or more.

summary: The Sages argue if a sukkah shaped like a tent with no flat roof is kosher. A reed mat may be used as s'chach only if it was made for s'chach and not for lying on.

chunks.en: Someone who makes his sukkah shaped like a pointed hut,
chunks.st: One who establishes his sukka like a type of circular hut,
chunks.stMore: with no roof whose walls slope down from the center

chunks.en: or leans it against a wall,
chunks.st: or who rested the sukka against the wall,
chunks.stMore: by taking long branches and placing one end on the ground and leaning the other end against the wall to establish a structure with no roof,

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says it is not kosher,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer deems it unfit

chunks.en: because it has no roof.
chunks.st: because it does not have a roof,

chunks.en: But the Sages say it is kosher.
chunks.st: and the Rabbis deem it fit;
chunks.stMore: as, in their opinion, the roof and the walls may be a single entity, indistinguishable from each other.

chunks.en: A big mat made of reeds:
chunks.st: In the case of a large mat of reeds,

chunks.en: if he made it for lying on,
chunks.st: if one initially produced it for the purpose of lying upon it,

chunks.en: it can become tamei, and may not be used as s'chach.
chunks.st: it is susceptible to ritual impurity like any other vessel, and therefore one may not roof a sukka with it.

chunks.he: לְסִכּוּךְ, מְסַכְּכִין בָּהּ וְאֵינָהּ מְקַבֶּלֶת טֻמְאָה.
chunks.en: If he made it for s'chach, it may be used as s'chach, and it cannot become tamei.
chunks.st: If one initially produced it for roofing, one may roof a sukka with it, and it is not susceptible to ritual impurity,
chunks.stMore: as its legal status is not that of a vessel.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says
chunks.stMore: that the distinction between mats is based on use, not size.

chunks.en: whether it is small or big,
chunks.st: Therefore, with regard to both a small mat and a large mat,

chunks.en: if he made it for lying on,
chunks.st: if one produced it for the purpose of lying upon it,

chunks.en: it can become tamei, and may not be used as s'chach.
chunks.st: it is susceptible to ritual impurity and one may not roof a sukka with it.

chunks.he: לְסִכּוּךְ, מְסַכְּכִין בָּהּ וְאֵינָהּ מְקַבֶּלֶת טֻמְאָה:
chunks.en: If he made it for s'chach, it may be used as s'chach, and it cannot become tamei.
chunks.st: If one produced it for roofing, one may roof a sukka with it, and it is not susceptible to ritual impurity.
